{"additions":2795,"baseRefName":"main","body":"## Summary

New source-only workspace package `@repo/knowledge` — the fully-tested MongoDB data layer for the knowledge hub (Plan 1 of 4). Mirrors `@repo/database` conventions; consumed by the upcoming ingestion backend (Plan 2), web surfaces (Plan 3), and ask-agent (Plan 4).

- **Schemas (Zod v4, single source of truth):** organizations, people, engagements, sources (voice/email/manual, incl. attachments), facts (≥1 anchor invariant, lifecycle convention: valid iff `validUntil` & `supersededBy` absent — exported as `currentlyValidFilter`), proposals (entity + fact drafts with pending/confirmed/edited/discarded resolutions)
- **Typed collections + idempotent indexes:** `getCollections(db)`, `ensureIndexes(db)`; every compound index leads with `tenantId`; unique gmail-message dedup via `partialFilterExpression`
- **GDPR Art. 17 erasure cascade:** `erasePerson` deletes person-anchored facts, redacts identifiers (full name, emails, and word-bounded name tokens incl. German genitive — Unicode-aware, since ASCII `\b` never fires before umlauts) in source texts *and* the proposal audit trail (open + resolved), discards pending drafts while leaving reviewed drafts' history intact, persists `blobsPendingDeletion` on orphaned-blob sources, and reports `orphanedBlobUrls` (audio + attachments) for caller-side deletion
- **Review write path:** `resolveProposalItems` — the single choke point that turns drafts into knowledge: strict-schema entity materialization, draft-anchor resolution (`organizationDraftId` → created entity), per-item confirm/edit/discard, proposal auto-resolve + source `reviewed`, idempotent re-run via deterministic `_id`s (crash-safe without transactions)
- **Search:** `facts_search` (with a `lucene.german` multi on `text`) + `organizations_search`/`people_search` for the resolve-context step and dedupe suggestions (3 indexes = exactly the M0 limit); pipeline builders for both; idempotent `setup-indexes` script with narrowed error handling
- **Runtime-portable entry points:** the barrel no longer transitively imports `server-only` (which throws in every non-react-server runtime — decisively, the Plan-2 eve app; reproduced from Bun tests). DB bootstrapping lives behind `@repo/knowledge/client` (house style, cf. `@repo/auth/server`) with an explicit browser guard and a configured client: `ignoreUndefined` (spreads with `undefined` lifecycle keys must not store BSON `null`), serverless pool/timeout right-sizing, `appName`

- Source discriminated-union modeling remains a fast-follow

New source-only workspace package `@repo/knowledge` — the fully-tested MongoDB data layer for the knowledge hub (Plan 1 of 4). Mirrors `@repo/database` conventions; consumed by the upcoming ingestion backend (Plan 2), web surfaces (Plan 3), and ask-agent (Plan 4).

- **Schemas (Zod v4, single source of truth):** organizations, people, engagements, sources (voice/email/manual, incl. attachments), facts (≥1 anchor invariant, lifecycle convention: valid iff `validUntil` & `supersededBy` absent — exported as `currentlyValidFilter`), proposals (entity + fact drafts with pending/confirmed/edited/discarded resolutions)

- **GDPR Art. 17 erasure cascade:** `erasePerson` deletes person-anchored facts, redacts identifiers (full name, emails, and word-bounded name tokens incl. German genitive — Unicode-aware, since ASCII `\b` never fires before umlauts) in source texts *and* the proposal audit trail (open + resolved), discards pending drafts while leaving reviewed drafts' history intact, persists `blobsPendingDeletion` on orphaned-blob sources, and reports `orphanedBlobUrls` (audio + attachments) for caller-side deletion

DB bootstrapping lives behind `@repo/knowledge/client` (house style, cf. `@repo/auth/server`) with an explicit browser guard and a configured client: `ignoreUndefined` (spreads with `undefined` lifecycle keys must not store BSON `null`), serverless pool/timeout right-sizing, `appName`

  erased person's audio forever.

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

Ported PR 292 (`feat(knowledge): @repo/knowledge data layer`) from `hasToggle/hasToggle.dev` into this repo (`hasToggle/spinor`), on branch `Kheirah/tacoma`.

## What moved

All 24 source files of the PR, applied verbatim as `packages/knowledge/`:

- **Schemas** (Zod v4) — `schemas/{shared,entities,facts,sources,proposals}.ts`: organizations, people, engagements, sources (voice/email/manual + attachments), facts (≥1 anchor invariant, `currentlyValidFilter` lifecycle convention), proposals (entity + fact drafts)
- **Collections & indexes** — `collections.ts`: `getCollections(db)`, `ensureIndexes(db)`, every compound index tenant-leading, gmail dedup via `partialFilterExpression`
- **GDPR Art. 17 cascade** — `erasure.ts`: `erasePerson` with Unicode-aware token redaction, proposal audit-trail redaction, `blobsPendingDeletion`, `orphanedBlobUrls`
- **Review write path** — `review.ts`: `resolveProposalItems`, deterministic `_id`s for crash-safe idempotent re-run
- **Search** — `search.ts` + `scripts/setup-indexes.ts`: `facts_search` (with `lucene.german` multi), `organizations_search`, `people_search`
- **Runtime-portable entry points** — barrel free of `server-only`; DB bootstrap behind `@repo/knowledge/client` with explicit browser guard and configured client (`ignoreUndefined`, serverless pool sizing)
- All 9 test files in `__tests__/`

## Deliberate deviations

- **`bun.lock` was not patched** — regenerated via `bun install` instead. Delta is exactly the `@repo/knowledge` workspace entry; no dependency drift elsewhere. The package's `mongodb@^7.5.0` / `zod@^4.4.3` / `@t3-oss/env-nextjs@^0.13.11` already match this repo's `@repo/database`, so nothing new was resolved.
- **The PR's three non-`knowledge` commits were no-ops here** (ultracite v7 biome preset paths, `entire` checkpoint routing, pinning check/fix off `@latest`) — they're absent from the PR's diff against main because this fork's main already carries them. Verified: root `package.json` already uses `bunx --bun ultracite check`.
- **Added a `@repo/knowledge` entry to `CLAUDE.md`**'s package list, since that file is the index new agents read.

## Verification (all run here, not inherited from the PR)

```
turbo typecheck --filter=@repo/knowledge   → 1 successful
biome check packages/knowledge             → 24 files, 0 errors
bun test (no MONGODB_TEST_URI)             → 29 pass, 30 skip, 0 fail
bun test (MONGODB_TEST_URI, mongo:8)       → 52 pass, 0 fail, 141 expect()
```

The Mongo run used a disposable `mongo:8` container on port 47017, now stopped and removed. 52/0 matches the PR's own reported result exactly.

## Two things to note

**Not committed.** The work is in the working tree (`packages/knowledge/` untracked, `CLAUDE.md` + `bun.lock` modified) so you can review it in Conductor's diff first. Say the word and I'll commit and open a PR against `main`.

**`CLAUDE.md` is stale beyond my edit.** It still documents `@repo/database` as "Prisma ORM with Neon PostgreSQL adapter" with a `schema.prisma` and a `bun migrate` workflow — but this repo's `@repo/database` is already MongoDB (`packages/database/index.ts` uses `MongoClient`, no Prisma anywhere). That predates this port, so I left it alone rather than widening scope, but it's worth a cleanup pass given spinor is now the MongoDB-native product repo.

The PR's deferred items carry over unchanged: Spike A (AssemblyAI EU smoke test) still blocked on credentials, source discriminated-union modeling is a fast-follow, and `resolveProposalItems` v1 still requires engagement drafts to carry a resolved `organizationId`.

feat(knowledge): @repo/knowledge data layer (port of hasToggle.dev#292)

Ports the knowledge-hub MongoDB data layer from hasToggle/hasToggle.dev#292
into spinor, which is where the company-brain product now lives; hasToggle.dev
goes back to being a Next.js & Vercel playground.

Source-only workspace package mirroring @repo/database conventions:

- Zod v4 schemas as the single source of truth: organizations, people,
  engagements, sources (voice/email/manual incl. attachments), facts (>=1
  anchor invariant; valid iff validUntil & supersededBy absent, exported as
  currentlyValidFilter), proposals (entity + fact drafts).
- Typed collections and idempotent indexes; every compound index leads with
  tenantId, gmail-message dedup is unique via partialFilterExpression.
- GDPR Art. 17 erasure cascade (erasePerson): deletes person-anchored facts,
  redacts identifiers in source texts and the proposal audit trail
  (Unicode-aware word boundaries incl. the German genitive, since ASCII \b
  never fires before umlauts), discards pending drafts while leaving reviewed
  drafts intact, persists blobsPendingDeletion and reports orphanedBlobUrls.
- resolveProposalItems: the single write-path choke point turning drafts into
  knowledge, idempotent via deterministic _ids (crash-safe without
  transactions).
- Atlas Search: facts_search (lucene.german multi on text) plus
  organizations_search / people_search, pipeline builders, and an idempotent
  setup-indexes script.
- Barrel stays free of server-only so it imports in any server runtime; DB
  bootstrapping lives behind @repo/knowledge/client with an explicit browser
  guard and a client configured for serverless (ignoreUndefined, pool and

message.content: wh could spinor as a name be appropriate to the idea of building a company brain? I'm kind of fascinated by the two rotations needed to start from the origin detail.

content.thinking:
The user is asking why "spinor" works as a name for this company-brain product, especially given the 720° rotation property. I need to connect the mathematical concept to the product architecture I've just built — explaining how spinors relate to rotations and why that's conceptually fitting for what this system does.

The core insight is that a spinor picks up a sign under a 2π rotation and needs a full 4π (720°) to return to its original state. This means spinors encode information about the path taken through rotation space, not just the endpoint — they're sensitive to the topology of the space in a way vectors aren't. Spinors are also "square roots" of vectors in a sense: you can construct observable vectors from spinor bilinears, but two spinors differing only by sign produce the same observable. This layering — where the underlying spinor structure is richer than what you can directly observe — mirrors how a company brain would work: the internal representation captures more nuance than what surfaces in the output.

Looking at the architecture I just ported, there's a striking parallel. The system doesn't jump directly from raw capture to knowledge. Instead it routes through source → proposal draft → human confirmation → fact, with facts anchored to organizations, people, and engagements. Facts are never deleted, only superseded, preserving the full history. This multi-step validation process is like the spinor's extra structure — the intermediate representations carry information that the final observable fact alone wouldn't. The human confirmation step is the measurement that collapses the proposal into a confirmed fact, much like how observing a spinor gives you a vector.

The second resonance is about path-dependence. A fact's current state includes its derivation history through the `supersededBy` field, so two databases with identical valid facts aren't equivalent if they arrived there differently. The system remembers not just what is true now, but how it became true. That's exactly the spinor property — the state depends on the path taken, not just the endpoint.

The third analogy is tighter structurally but I should note it's a bit more speculative: spinors are square roots of vectors, and observables require pairing two spinors together. Similarly, a fact only becomes observable knowledge when paired with its anchor and source — the claim alone isn't enough. Your requirement that every fact carry at least one anchor is a refusal to store unpaired objects.

The fourth point concerns sign and phase. A spinor's absolute sign is unobservable in isolation, but the relative sign between spinors in superposition matters physically. I'm drawing a parallel to how individual fact signs might not be observable in isolation, but their relative relationships are what create meaning in the system.

The fifth analogy is about the double cover structure — spinors can't be derived from SO(3) alone; you need the larger Spin(3) group. The extra structure isn't observable from the rotation group itself, which mirrors how your provenance metadata isn't derivable from the observable facts alone.

The sixth point is a cautionary note: spinors' defining property is that a 2π rotation is physically indistinguishable from no rotation for an isolated spinor — the sign is just a gauge artifact. If someone pushed the analogy too hard, they'd argue the review step changes nothing observable, which contradicts your thesis. So the metaphor works best at the level of path-dependence and double cover, not as a statement about what the minus sign means. There's also the GDPR erasure consideration to keep in mind.

`erasePerson` is genuinely different from everything else in the system — it's the only non-unitary operation, an irreversible projection that destroys information rather than preserving history like supersession and proposals do. In quantum terms, it's measurement and collapse rather than unitary evolution. The design acknowledges this discomfort by reporting orphaned blob URLs and persisting blobs pending deletion, trying to make an irreversible operation at least traceable and accountable. And there's the colloquial sense of "spin" that a company brain has to navigate too.

Unit quaternions are probably the most concrete spinor model most programmers have actually encountered through 3D graphics code — the fact that q and −q represent the same rotation is a nice intuitive grounding for explaining why the name makes sense to a developer audience. The belt trick is also a tangible way to explain it to non-technical people.

For the format, I'm thinking conversational and prose-heavy rather than a checklist, with maybe some bold lead-ins for the main resonances but mostly flowing paragraphs. The user wants depth without an unbounded essay. I should double-check the math: SO(3)'s fundamental group is ℤ₂, and the 2:1 map from SU(2) to SO(3) works because SU(2) is isomorphic to S³. I'm going to skip saving this to memory since it's my own reasoning about the naming rather than an established fact about their project intent. Time to write the response.

content.text:
It fits better than most product names do, and the 720° detail is exactly the load-bearing part.

**The double cover is the shape of your write path.** A spinor lives in a representation of Spin(n), the double cover of the rotation group. Rotate it by 2π and it doesn't come back — it comes back as *minus itself*. Only the second full turn restores it. The reason is topological: SO(3) has fundamental group ℤ/2, so a 360° loop in rotation space is not contractible, while the 720° loop is. Spinors are the objects that can tell the difference.

That's structurally the same statement as the core decision in the data layer I just ported. A source does not become a fact in one step. Extraction gets you to something that *looks* like knowledge and sits in exactly the right place — same entity, same claim, same anchors — but carries the opposite sign. It's a proposal. The second rotation, human confirmation through `resolveProposalItems`, is what returns it to identity. A system that treated one turn as sufficient is an LLM writing straight into a database. Naming the product after the class of object for which one turn is provably not enough is a fairly precise piece of self-description.

**Path-dependence is the other half.** A spinor's state depends on the route taken, not just the endpoint. Two spinors at the same orientation can differ by sign because one got there the long way. Your fact model does this deliberately: `supersededBy` and `validUntil` mean the currently-valid set carries its own derivation. Two knowledge bases with identical current facts are *not* the same knowledge base if one arrived by supersession and the other by assertion. A company brain that stored only current state would be storing vectors. You're storing spinors.

**And the sign only matters relationally** — which is the subtle part, and the part that saves the metaphor from being decorative. The overall sign of a single isolated spinor is unobservable. What's observable is the *relative* sign between two of them. This isn't hand-waving: Rauch and Werner independently measured it in 1975 by splitting a neutron beam, rotating one arm through 2π, and watching the interference pattern invert. Same in your system. No single fact's provenance matters much on its own. The moment two accounts of the same engagement disagree, `confirmedBy` and the retained proposal trail stop being overhead and become the entire answer. That's why proposals survive resolution instead of being deleted — the extra structure can't be reconstructed from the observables, exactly as spinors can't be built from SO(3) alone.

There's a nice practical bonus: every graphics programmer has already handled a spinor without calling it that. Unit quaternions are the concrete model, and everyone who's written rotation code knows *q* and *−q* give the same rotation. And for non-technical explanation you get the belt trick — hand someone a belt, put one twist in it, watch them fail to remove it without releasing the ends, then add a second twist and watch it fall out. Having a physical demo of your product thesis is not nothing.

**Where I'd stop pushing it.** The honest seam is that for a single isolated spinor, the 2π state is *physically indistinguishable* from the 0 state — the sign is gauge in isolation. Pushed too hard, the metaphor implies the review step changes nothing observable, which inverts your thesis. Hold it at path-dependence and the double cover, not at "the minus sign is bad."

The genuinely interesting break is `erasePerson`. Everything else in that data layer is information-preserving — supersession retains, resolution retains, the audit trail retains. GDPR erasure is the one operation that irreversibly destroys state. In the analogy it isn't a rotation at all; it's the measurement, the non-unitary step. And it's telling that the implementation is visibly uncomfortable about it: persisting `blobsPendingDeletion`, reporting `orphanedBlobUrls`, redacting rather than dropping the proposal history. It can't make the operation reversible, so it settles for making it accountable. That's the one place the name stops describing the system — which is probably the right place for a naming metaphor to break.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/eric/.claude/skills/get-api-docs

# Get API Docs via chub

When you need documentation for a library or API, fetch it with the `chub` CLI
rather than guessing from training data. This gives you the current, correct API.

## Step 1 — Find the right doc ID

```bash
chub search "<library name>" --json
```

Pick the best-matching `id` from the results (e.g. `openai/chat`, `anthropic/sdk`,
`stripe/api`). If nothing matches, try a broader term.

## Step 2 — Fetch the docs

```bash
chub get <id> --lang py    # or --lang js, --lang ts
```

Omit `--lang` if the doc has only one language variant — it will be auto-selected.

## Step 3 — Use the docs

Read the fetched content and use it to write accurate code or answer the question.
Do not rely on memorized API shapes — use what the docs say.

## Step 4 — Annotate what you learned

After completing the task, if you discovered something not in the doc — a gotcha,
workaround, version quirk, or project-specific detail — save it so future sessions
start smarter:

```bash
chub annotate <id> "Webhook verification requires raw body — do not parse before verifying"
```

Annotations are local, persist across sessions, and appear automatically on future
`chub get` calls. Keep notes concise and actionable. Don't repeat what's already in
the doc.

## Step 5 — Give feedback

Rate the doc so authors can improve it. Ask the user before sending.

```bash
chub feedback <id> up                        # doc worked well
chub feedback <id> down --label outdated     # doc needs updating
```

Available labels: `outdated`, `inaccurate`, `incomplete`, `wrong-examples`,
`wrong-version`, `poorly-structured`, `accurate`, `well-structured`, `helpful`,
`good-examples`.

## Quick reference

| Goal | Command |
|------|---------|
| List everything | `chub search` |
| Find a doc | `chub search "stripe"` |
| Exact id detail | `chub search stripe/api` |
| Fetch Python docs | `chub get stripe/api --lang py` |
| Fetch JS docs | `chub get openai/chat --lang js` |
| Save to file | `chub get anthropic/sdk --lang py -o docs.md` |
| Fetch multiple | `chub get openai/chat stripe/api --lang py` |
| Save a note | `chub annotate stripe/api "needs raw body"` |
| List notes | `chub annotate --list` |
| Rate a doc | `chub feedback stripe/api up` |

## Notes

- `chub search` with no query lists everything available
- IDs are `<author>/<name>` — confirm the ID from search before fetching
- If multiple languages exist and you don't pass `--lang`, chub will tell you which are available

# GitHub App Permissions and Token Requirements for Self-Hosted Renovate

## Required Permissions

When creating a self-hosted GitHub App for Renovate, these permissions are mandatory:

| Permission | Scope |
|-----------|-------|
| Checks | `read` + `write` |
| Commit statuses | `read` + `write` |
| Contents | `read` + `write` |
| Issues | `read` + `write` |
| Pull requests | `read` + `write` |
| Workflows | `read` + `write` |
| Administration | `read` |
| Dependabot alerts | `read` |
| Members | `read` |
| Metadata | `read` |

## Installation Token Details

**Token Type**: You must use "a [GitHub App Installation token](https://docs.github.com/en/developers/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps#authenticating-as-an-installation)" rather than a standard PAT.

**Token Lifespan**: Installation tokens "expire after 1 hour and need to be regenerated regularly."

**Token Format**: Tokens starting with `ghs_` don't require prefixes. However, tokens from GitHub Enterprise Server versions before 3.2 must be prefixed with `x-access-token:`.

## Configuration Methods

Supply the token through any of these approaches:
- `token` parameter in `config.js`
- `RENOVATE_TOKEN` environment variable
- CLI `--token=` parameter

Note: The documentation does not mention a `GITHUB_COM_TOKEN` environment variable specifically for this configuration.

content.content:
# Current Recommended Usage of renovatebot/github-action

## Key Inputs

The action accepts several important inputs:

- **token**: A Personal Access Token (classic) with `repo` scope for public and private repositories
- **configurationFile**: JavaScript or JSON configuration file for global Renovate settings
- **renovate-version**: Specifies which Renovate version to use (defaults to a pinch version)
- **env-regex**: Pattern matching which environment variables pass to the container
- **docker-*** options**: For customizing Docker container behavior (user, volumes, socket mounting, etc.)

## Using a GitHub App Token

Rather than a personal access token tied to an individual, you can implement a GitHub App for better permission control. The recommended approach uses the `actions/create-github-app-token` action:

```yaml
- name: Get token
  id: get_token
  uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v1
  with:
    private-key: ${{ secrets.private_key }}
    app-id: ${{ secrets.app_id }}
    owner: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
    repositories: 'repo1,repo2'
```

Then pass this token to the Renovate action as `token: '${{ steps.get_token.outputs.token }}'`.

## Complete Example Workflow

```yaml
name: Renovate
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0/15 * * * *'
jobs:
  renovate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v6.1.0
      - name: Self-hosted Renovate
        uses: renovatebot/github-action@v46.1.21
        with:
          configurationFile: example/renovate-config.js
          token: ${{ secrets.RENOVATE_TOKEN }}
```

This basic workflow runs every 15 minutes and requires the `RENOVATE_TOKEN` secret to be configured in your repository settings.

# Renovate's Bun Support

**File Matching:**
Renovate automatically detects bun projects by matching `"/(^|/)bun\.lockb?$/"` and `"/(^|/)package\.json$/"`. This means it recognizes both `bun.lock` and `bun.lockb` files.

**Lock File Maintenance:**
Yes, the manager supports lock file maintenance for both `bun.lockb` and `bun.lock`. The documentation notes that `"Lock file maintenance is delegated to the underlying package manager, which Renovate runs as an external command."` This indicates Renovate invokes bun directly to update lock files.

**Datasources:**
The manager supports extracting dependencies from npm and GitHub tags datasources.

**Important Caveat:**
When a `package.json` is found as part of bun results, it gets excluded from npm manager processing—*unless* an npm/pnpm/Yarn lock file is also present. This prevents duplicate processing.

**Not Addressed:**
The documentation provided doesn't mention workspace support, bun binary availability requirements, or other potential caveats beyond the package.json exclusion behavior noted above.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Renovate's `forkProcessing` configuration:

## forkProcessing Default Behavior

When an Organization installs Renovate with the "All repositories" option, forkProcessing will remain set to its default value "disabled", which means forked repositories are not onboarded and Renovate ignores them.

## For Self-Hosted Renovate

If an Organization installs Renovate with "Selected repositories", it's assumed the organization wants to onboard all selected repositories including forked ones, so forkProcessing is set to "enabled".

## Enabling forkProcessing for Explicitly Configured Repositories

For forked repositories that are explicitly configured, to change the default behavior, you should push a renovate.json file to the repository with `"forkProcessing": "enabled"`.

The key distinction is that when using "All repositories" installation, forked repositories are ignored by default, but this can be changed by adding a renovate.json configuration file with the appropriate fork processing setting.

This means that for self-hosted setups where repositories are explicitly configured, the default "auto" behavior determines whether forks are processed based on how the repository was selected during installation or configuration.

name: Renovate

# Self-hosted replacement for the Mend Cloud Runner that drives hasToggle.dev.
# The bot identity is a GitHub App owned by the org (see docs/renovate.md);
# nothing here depends on a human's personal access token.

on:
  schedule:
    # Every four hours. This only controls how often Renovate wakes up and
    # looks — what it is allowed to open is decided by renovate.json.
    - cron: "0 */4 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      logLevel:
        description: Log level
        type: choice
        default: info
        options:
          - debug
          - info
          - warn
      dryRun:
        description: Dry run — resolve everything, write nothing
        type: boolean
        default: false

# Two overlapping runs duplicate branch work and can race each other's
# automerge step. Queue rather than cancel so a scheduled tick is never lost.
concurrency:
  group: renovate
  cancel-in-progress: false

# The job's own GITHUB_TOKEN does nothing here — every write goes through the
# App installation token minted below.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  renovate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Mint an App installation token
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v3
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RENOVATE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RENOVATE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          owner: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
          repositories: ${{ github.event.repository.name }}

      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # Renovate clones the repo itself with the App token; the checkout is
          # only here to give the action a workspace. Leaving the Actions
          # credentials behind in .git/config would serve no purpose.
          persist-credentials: false

      # Setting the env var only when the input is true keeps RENOVATE_DRY_RUN
      # absent on normal runs — an empty string is not a valid dryRun value.
      - name: Enable dry run
        if: ${{ inputs.dryRun }}
        run: echo "RENOVATE_DRY_RUN=full" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Renovate
        uses: renovatebot/github-action@v46.2.0
        with:
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          # Floats within the major so patches arrive without a config bump;
          # Renovate keeps the `uses:` pin above current by itself.
          renovate-version: 44
        env:
          # Global (self-hosted) config lives here rather than in a config file
          # so there is one place to read. The action forwards any RENOVATE_*
          # and LOG_LEVEL vars into the container.
          RENOVATE_PLATFORM: github
          RENOVATE_REPOSITORIES: ${{ github.repository }}
          # renovate.json is already committed, so the onboarding-PR flow is
          # dead weight — and requiring config means a run against a repo
          # without one fails loudly instead of silently doing nothing.
          RENOVATE_ONBOARDING: "false"
          RENOVATE_REQUIRE_CONFIG: required
          LOG_LEVEL: ${{ inputs.logLevel || 'info' }}

# Renovate (self-hosted)

`hasToggle.dev` is kept current by the Mend-hosted Renovate Cloud Runner. This
repo is not installed on that app, so it runs its own Renovate from
`.github/workflows/renovate.yml`, authenticated as an org-owned GitHub App.

Dependency policy itself lives in `renovate.json` at the repo root and is
unchanged from the upstream template. This document only covers the runner.

## Why a GitHub App rather than a PAT

- The token is a short-lived installation token (1 hour), minted per run, not a
  long-lived secret tied to a person's account.
- Pull requests are authored by the app, not by whoever's PAT it is, so
  `git log` and the PR list stay honest about what is automation.
- The app has its own API rate limit rather than sharing a human's.
- **Pull requests opened with an App token trigger other workflows.** Ones
  opened with the job's built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not — CI would never run on
  a Renovate PR, and with `automerge: true` that means merging unverified.

## One-time setup

### 1. Create the App

Requires org-owner rights on `hasToggle`. The permission list is long and
getting one wrong fails at run time rather than at setup, so use the manifest
form generated at `.context/renovate-app-manifest.html` — open it in a browser
and it posts a pre-filled app definition to GitHub. Otherwise, create it by hand
at **Organization settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps → New GitHub App**

content.text:
**PR #2: https://github.com/hasToggle/spinor/pull/2** — `Kheirah/self-hosted-renovate` → `main`. Also switched `origin` to `git@github.com:hasToggle/spinor.git` as you asked (which incidentally fixed the push problem from earlier — and was necessary here, since the `gh` token lacks `workflow` scope and would have rejected a workflow file over HTTPS).

## What landed

`.github/workflows/renovate.yml` — four-hour schedule + `workflow_dispatch` with `logLevel` and `dryRun` inputs, concurrency that queues rather than cancels, global config as `RENOVATE_*` env vars instead of a config file. `docs/renovate.md` — the one-time setup. `renovate.json` — one added line.

Verified with `actionlint` (clean) and the official `renovate-config-validator` (accepts the config).

## Why a GitHub App, concretely

Beyond token hygiene, there's a decisive reason given your existing config: **PRs opened with the job's built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger other workflows.** Your `renovate.json` already has `automerge: true` for patch and minor. With a `GITHUB_TOKEN`-authored PR, `claude-code-review.yml` and friends would never fire, and Renovate would merge PRs that no CI ever saw. An App installation token does trigger them.

## Three things I found that you'll want to decide on

**`renovate.json` needed `forkProcessing: "enabled"`.** spinor is a fork of hasToggle.dev, and Renovate skips forks by default. Without this the runner would have started, found the repo, and silently done nothing — the worst failure mode, since it looks like it's working.

**Issues are disabled on this repo.** Forks get Issues off by default. `config:recommended` enables the Dependency Dashboard, which Renovate maintains *as an issue* — so it'll log an error every run and you lose the best view of what's pending. Either `gh api -X PATCH repos/hasToggle/spinor -f has_issues=true` or set `"dependencyDashboard": false` deliberately.

**Auto-merge is off and `main` is unprotected.** Renovate prefers GitHub's native auto-merge; with the repo setting off it falls back to merging patch/minor PRs itself on its next run — *without waiting for CI*, since there's no required check to wait on. Combined with `automerge: true`, that's unreviewed, untested merges every four hours. `gh api -X PATCH repos/hasToggle/spinor -f allow_auto_merge=true` plus a required status check on `main` closes it.

I left all three repo settings as I found them — they're settings, not code, and yours to call. The `forkProcessing` line is in the PR because it's config that belongs in the repo.

## One hypothesis I had to drop

I was going to fix `"packageManager": "bun@1.1.43"` in the root `package.json`, on the theory that Renovate would install that bun to regenerate `bun.lock` — and bun 1.1.43 predates the text lockfile format the repo actually uses. I checked Renovate's `bun/artifacts.ts` first: it selects the bun version from `constraints.bun`, not from `packageManager`. With no constraint set it installs current bun, which handles the text lockfile fine. So no change was needed and I made none. The declaration *is* stale (you're on 1.3.14 locally), but that's unrelated cleanup — say the word if you want it in a separate PR.

## To make it live

1. Open `.context/renovate-app-manifest.html` in a browser — it posts a pre-filled app definition to GitHub so you don't hand-set ten permissions. (Untracked, per Conductor convention.)
2. Generate a private key, note the App ID, install on `hasToggle/spinor` only.
3. `gh secret set RENOVATE_APP_ID` and `gh secret set RENOVATE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`.
4. `gh workflow run renovate.yml -f dryRun=true -f logLevel=debug` to validate before it writes anything.

One housekeeping note: those 31 SVGs reformatted themselves again in the working tree between my two branches. Something in this workspace is still running a floating ultracite despite the root scripts being pinned — worth tracking down separately, since it'll keep polluting every branch you touch.

Sources: [Renovate GitHub platform docs](https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/platform/github/), [renovatebot/github-action](https://github.com/renovatebot/github-action), [Renovate self-hosted config](https://docs.renovatebot.com/self-hosted-configuration/), [Renovate bun manager](https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/manager/bun/)

# Renovate (self-hosted)

`hasToggle.dev` is kept current by the Mend-hosted Renovate Cloud Runner. This
repo is not installed on that app, so it runs its own Renovate from
`.github/workflows/renovate.yml`, authenticated as an org-owned GitHub App.

Dependency policy itself lives in `renovate.json` at the repo root and is
unchanged from the upstream template. This document only covers the runner.

## Why a GitHub App rather than a PAT

- The token is a short-lived installation token (1 hour), minted per run, not a
  long-lived secret tied to a person's account.
- Pull requests are authored by the app, not by whoever's PAT it is, so
  `git log` and the PR list stay honest about what is automation.
- The app has its own API rate limit rather than sharing a human's.
- **Pull requests opened with an App token trigger other workflows.** Ones
  opened with the job's built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not — CI would never run on
  a Renovate PR, and with `automerge: true` that means merging unverified.

## One-time setup

### 1. Create the App

Requires org-owner rights on `hasToggle`. The permission list is long and
getting one wrong fails at run time rather than at setup, so use the manifest
form generated at `.context/renovate-app-manifest.html` — open it in a browser
and it posts a pre-filled app definition to GitHub. Otherwise, create it by hand
at **Organization settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps → New GitHub App**
with exactly these permissions ([source](https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/platform/github/)):

| Permission                  | Access       |
| --------------------------- | ------------ |
| Administration              | Read         |
| Checks                      | Read & write |
| Commit statuses             | Read & write |
| Contents                    | Read & write |
| Dependabot alerts           | Read         |
| Issues                      | Read & write |
| Members (organization)      | Read         |
| Metadata                    | Read         |
| Pull requests               | Read & write |
| Workflows                   | Read & write |

Subscribe to no events — this runner polls on a schedule and needs no webhook.
`Workflows: write` is what lets Renovate bump action versions inside
`.github/workflows/`; without it those updates fail while everything else
succeeds, which is a confusing way to find out.

### 2. Generate a private key and note the App ID

On the app's settings page: **Generate a private key** (downloads a `.pem`) and
copy the numeric **App ID** from the top of the page.

### 3. Install the App on this repo

**Install App → hasToggle → Only select repositories → `spinor`**.

### 4. Add the secrets

```sh
gh secret set RENOVATE_APP_ID          --repo hasToggle/spinor --body '<app id>'
gh secret set RENOVATE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY --repo hasToggle/spinor < ~/Downloads/<app>.private-key.pem
```

Then delete the local `.pem` — it can always be regenerated, and a key sitting
in `~/Downloads` is a standing liability.

### 5. Verify

```sh
gh workflow run renovate.yml --repo hasToggle/spinor -f dryRun=true -f logLevel=debug
gh run watch --repo hasToggle/spinor
```

A dry run resolves every update and writes nothing. Look for
`Repository started` and a `DRY-RUN` line per branch it would have created. Then
run it again without `dryRun` to let it open real PRs.

## Repo settings this depends on

Two settings are off on this repo and both change how `automerge: true` behaves:

- **Issues are disabled.** `config:recommended` turns on the Dependency
  Dashboard, which Renovate maintains as an issue. With Issues off it logs an
  error every run and you lose the single best view of what is pending. Fix
  with `gh api -X PATCH repos/hasToggle/spinor -f has_issues=true`, or set
  `"dependencyDashboard": false` in `renovate.json` to opt out deliberately.
- **Auto-merge is disabled, and `main` is unprotected.** Renovate prefers
  GitHub's native auto-merge, which needs the repo setting on *and* something
  blocking the merge (a required check) for it to mean anything. With neither,
  Renovate falls back to merging patch and minor PRs itself on its next run —
  without waiting for CI. If that is not what you want, enable auto-merge and
  protect `main` with a required check:

  ```sh
  gh api -X PATCH repos/hasToggle/spinor -f allow_auto_merge=true
  ```

## Notes

- `forkProcessing: "enabled"` in `renovate.json` is load-bearing: this repo is a
  fork of `hasToggle.dev`, and Renovate skips forks by default.
- Cost is not a concern — the repo is public, so Actions minutes are free.
- To pause the bot without deleting anything, disable the workflow:
  `gh workflow disable renovate.yml --repo hasToggle/spinor`.

# Renovate (self-hosted)

`hasToggle.dev` is kept current by the Mend-hosted Renovate Cloud Runner. This
repo is not installed on that app, so it runs its own Renovate from
`.github/workflows/renovate.yml`, authenticated as an org-owned GitHub App.

Dependency policy itself lives in `renovate.json` at the repo root and is
unchanged from the upstream template. This document only covers the runner.

## Why a GitHub App rather than a PAT

- The token is a short-lived installation token (1 hour), minted per run, not a
  long-lived secret tied to a person's account.
- Pull requests are authored by the app, not by whoever's PAT it is, so
  `git log` and the PR list stay honest about what is automation.
- The app has its own API rate limit rather than sharing a human's.
- **Pull requests opened with an App token trigger other workflows.** Ones
  opened with the job's built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not — CI would never run on
  a Renovate PR, and with `automerge: true` that means merging unverified.

## One-time setup

### 1. Create the App

Requires org-owner rights on `hasToggle`. The permission list is long and
getting one wrong fails at run time rather than at setup, so use the manifest
form generated at `.context/renovate-app-manifest.html` — open it in a browser
and it posts a pre-filled app definition to GitHub. Otherwise, create it by hand
at **Organization settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps → New GitHub App**
with exactly these permissions ([source](https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/platform/github/)):

The form groups these under **Repository permissions** and **Organization
permissions**, and it labels several of them differently from the API keys used
in the manifest — which is worth knowing if you are cross-reading the two.

| Section      | Label on the form | API key               | Access       |
| ------------ | ----------------- | --------------------- | ------------ |
| Repository   | Administration    | `administration`      | Read         |
| Repository   | Checks            | `checks`              | Read & write |
| Repository   | Commit statuses   | `statuses`            | Read & write |
| Repository   | Contents          | `contents`            | Read & write |
| Repository   | Dependabot alerts | `vulnerability_alerts`| Read         |
| Repository   | Issues            | `issues`              | Read & write |
| Repository   | Metadata          | `metadata`            | Read         |
| Repository   | Pull requests     | `pull_requests`       | Read & write |
| Repository   | Workflows         | `workflows`           | Read & write |
| Organization | Members           | `members`             | Read         |

The two that are hardest to find are `statuses`, which the form calls **Commit
statuses**, and `vulnerability_alerts`, which it calls **Dependabot alerts**.
`members` is not in the Repository list at all — scroll down to the separate
Organization permissions section.

Sanity check: `gh api /apps/renovate --jq .permissions` returns the permission
set of Mend's own hosted Renovate app. It matches the table above, plus
`emails: read` and `packages: read`, which the docs do not list as required.

Subscribe to no events — this runner polls on a schedule and needs no webhook.
`Workflows: write` is what lets Renovate bump action versions inside
`.github/workflows/`; without it those updates fail while everything else
succeeds, which is a confusing way to find out.

### 2. Generate a private key and note the App ID

On the app's settings page: **Generate a private key** (downloads a `.pem`) and
copy the numeric **App ID** from the top of the page.

### 3. Install the App on this repo

**Install App → hasToggle → Only select repositories → `spinor`**.

### 4. Add the secrets

```sh
gh secret set RENOVATE_APP_ID          --repo hasToggle/spinor --body '<app id>'
gh secret set RENOVATE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY --repo hasToggle/spinor < ~/Downloads/<app>.private-key.pem
```

Then delete the local `.pem` — it can always be regenerated, and a key sitting
in `~/Downloads` is a standing liability.

### 5. Verify

```sh
gh workflow run renovate.yml --repo hasToggle/spinor -f dryRun=true -f logLevel=debug
gh run watch --repo hasToggle/spinor
```

A dry run resolves every update and writes nothing. Look for
`Repository started` and a `DRY-RUN` line per branch it would have created. Then
run it again without `dryRun` to let it open real PRs.

## Repo settings this depends on

Two settings are off on this repo and both change how `automerge: true` behaves:

- **Issues are disabled.** `config:recommended` turns on the Dependency
  Dashboard, which Renovate maintains as an issue. With Issues off it logs an
  error every run and you lose the single best view of what is pending. Fix
  with `gh api -X PATCH repos/hasToggle/spinor -f has_issues=true`, or set
  `"dependencyDashboard": false` in `renovate.json` to opt out deliberately.
- **Auto-merge is disabled, `main` is unprotected, and no workflow runs on
  pull requests.** Renovate prefers GitHub's native auto-merge, which needs the
  repo setting on *and* something blocking the merge (a required check) for it
  to mean anything. With none of the three, `automerge: true` in
  `renovate.json` means patch and minor dependency updates land on `main` with
  no automated verification whatsoever — Renovate merges them itself on its
  next run. That may well be the intended trade for a repo reviewed locally,
  but it should be a decision rather than a discovery. To close it, add a CI
  workflow on `pull_request`, require it on `main`, and:

  ```sh
  gh api -X PATCH repos/hasToggle/spinor -f allow_auto_merge=true
  ```

## Notes

- `forkProcessing: "enabled"` in `renovate.json` is load-bearing: this repo is a
  fork of `hasToggle.dev`, and Renovate skips forks by default.
- Cost is not a concern — the repo is public, so Actions minutes are free.
- To pause the bot without deleting anything, disable the workflow:
  `gh workflow disable renovate.yml --repo hasToggle/spinor`.

## Why you couldn't find those two permissions

My manifest used **API keys**; the form shows **different labels**. Nothing was wrong with the keys — they were just spelled differently on screen:

- `statuses` → **"Commit statuses"**
- `vulnerability_alerts` → **"Dependabot alerts"**

All of this is now in `docs/renovate.md`, and I deleted the manifest HTML: posting it from a `file://` origin gets rejected, which is why the button did nothing for you.

## Something you should fix in this workspace

`.claude/settings.json` has a `Stop` hook:

```json
"command": "bunx --bun biome format --write . 2>/dev/null; exit 0"
```

That reformats **the entire repo** after every turn I take, which is what's been reformatting those 31 SVGs over and over. It's not ultracite floating to v8 as your hasToggle.dev commit assumed — it's this hook, and the `2>/dev/null; exit 0` means it never reports what it touched. 2. `gh secret set RENOVATE_APP_ID` / `gh secret set RENOVATE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, then delete the local `.pem`.
3. `gh api /apps/spinor-renovate --jq '{permissions, events}'` to confirm what GitHub actually saved.
4. `gh workflow run renovate.yml -f dryRun=true -f logLevel=debug` before letting it write.

One consequence of dropping `claude-code-review.yml` that I put in the PR body: it was the only `pull_request`-triggered workflow (`claude.yml` only fires on comments and reviews). So nothing runs on PRs now, and with `automerge: true`, no branch protection, and `allow_auto_merge` off, Renovate will merge patch and minor updates itself with no automated check at all. Reasonable if you're reviewing locally — just make sure it's a choice.

content.text:
Both answered concretely:

## 1. No collision

`hasToggle/spinor` currently has **zero** repo secrets, so there's nothing to overwrite. More importantly, secrets are namespaced by where they live:

| Where the secret lives | Visible to |
|---|---|
| Repo secret on `hasToggle/spinor` | only workflows in that repo |
| Secrets in your other org | only that org's repos — **completely separate store** |

My commands use `--repo hasToggle/spinor`, so they create repo-scoped secrets. A Renovate app in a different org can't see them and they can't see it. Same names, different namespaces, no interference — much like two `.env` files in two projects both having `DATABASE_URL`.

The one overlap case is if `hasToggle` itself has an **org-level** secret with the same name shared to spinor. Even then it's not an error: repo secrets take precedence over org secrets, so the one I set would win — which is what you'd want. I couldn't verify that; your `gh` token lacks `admin:org` and got a 403. To check: `gh auth refresh -h github.com -s admin:org` then `gh secret list --org hasToggle`.

Also worth knowing: the App ID and private key are a matched pair. Your other app's key won't authenticate as this one, so mixing them up fails loudly rather than doing something subtle.

*(If your existing app happens to be set to "Any account" installability, you could install that one on spinor and reuse its credentials instead of creating a second app. I'd advise against it — one credential spanning two orgs means a rotation or compromise hits both.)*

## 2. The .pem — pipe it, don't paste it

Pipe the file straight in. This preserves the newlines exactly, which matters:

```sh
gh secret set RENOVATE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY --repo hasToggle/spinor \
  < ~/Downloads/spinor-renovate.*.private-key.pem
```

If you use the web UI instead, paste the **entire** contents including the `-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----` and `-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----` lines — not just the base64 body.

Three things that bite people:

- **Don't base64-encode it.** `create-github-app-token` does not decode base64 for you; its README shows you doing the `base64 -d` yourself in a prior step. Raw PEM is what it wants. (It does auto-convert escaped `\n` into real newlines, so a mangled paste sometimes still works — but don't rely on that.)
- **App ID is the numeric one** at the top of the app settings page, not the `Iv1.…` Client ID.
- **Delete the local `.pem` afterwards.** You can't re-download it. If you lose it, generate a new key on the app page and delete the old one — that's routine, not a disaster.

The App ID isn't actually sensitive (it's visible to anyone who can see the app), but keeping it as a secret alongside the key is harmless and keeps the workflow uniform.

Want me to add a short "private key" note to `docs/renovate.md` so this is written down for next time? It's a two-minute commit and PR #2 is still open.

Here's where things stand while the dry run pulls the image.

## Confirmations — two pass, two blockers

**Secrets are set correctly:**
```
RENOVATE_APP_ID           2026-08-01T14:40:27Z
RENOVATE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY  2026-08-01T14:41:22Z
```

**The app is exactly right** — `gh api /apps/spinor-renovate` returns all ten permissions and zero events, matching the spec with nothing extra.

**Blocker 1 — the app was created but never installed.** `gh api /orgs/hasToggle/installations` lists `vercel`, `mintlify`, `renovate`, `entire`, `claude` — no `spinor-renovate`. Creating an app and installing it are separate steps. Go to the app's settings → **Install App** → `hasToggle` → Only select repositories → `spinor`.

**Blocker 2 — the workflow isn't on `main` yet.** `workflow_dispatch` only registers once the file is on the default branch, so `gh workflow run renovate.yml` can't work while PR #2 is open. `gh workflow list` currently shows only `Claude Code Review`. **Merging PR #2 is your call — say the word and I'll merge it.**

That's why I started a *local* dry run instead: `renovate/renovate:44` in Docker with `RENOVATE_DRY_RUN=full`, using your existing `gh` token. It writes nothing — no branches, no PRs, no issues. It validates config, fork processing, and bun extraction, so you get a real signal without waiting on the two blockers. I'll report when it lands.

## Incidental finding

Mend's hosted `renovate` app **is already installed on the `hasToggle` org** with "selected repositories" — that's what drives hasToggle.dev. Adding `spinor` to that installation is one click and needs no workflow, no App, and no secrets. You asked specifically to self-host so I built that, and self-hosting does give you version control over the runner and no third-party in the loop. But if the Cloud Runner is fine, the simpler path is sitting right there.

## When the dashboard appears — it currently never will

`has_issues` is still `false` on spinor, and the Dependency Dashboard *is* a GitHub issue. With Issues disabled, Renovate can't create it — it'll log an error each run and you get no dashboard at all.

I double-checked the enablement chain rather than trusting a docs summary that claimed otherwise. Read straight out of the installed package:

```
config:recommended → extends [":dependencyDashboard", ...]
```

So it's on via your `extends: ["config:recommended"]`. Once Issues are enabled, the issue titled **"Dependency Dashboard"** is created on the first non-dry-run where Renovate has something to report, then updated in place on every run afterward — it's a single long-lived issue, not one per update. Dry runs never create it, so today's local run won't produce one either.

To turn it on: `gh api -X PATCH repos/hasToggle/spinor -f has_issues=true`. Or if you'd rather not have Issues on this repo at all, set `"dependencyDashboard": false` in `renovate.json` so Renovate stops trying and stops erroring.

Worth noting these interact: with automerge on and no CI, the dashboard is the only place you'd see what Renovate is doing before it lands on `main`. Turning Issues off and leaving automerge on means updates merge with neither a check nor a visible queue.

**`forkProcessing: "enabled"` was necessary and works.** `enabled: true, onboarded: true` — Renovate processed the fork instead of skipping it. That was the silent-no-op risk, and it's now confirmed closed by observation rather than by reading docs.

**The bun manager reads your monorepo correctly** — 379 dependencies across 28 `package.json` files. No lockfile complaints, so the text `bun.lock` is fine and my earlier decision not to pin `constraints.bun` holds.

**`github-actions` found 2 files, 6 deps** — that's `claude.yml` and `claude-code-review.yml` as they exist on `main` today. This is what `workflows: write` is for.

**Nothing to update right now.** No "would create branch/PR" lines at all — your recent Renovate PRs (#332–#336) brought everything current. So when the real runner does fire, expect zero PRs on the first pass. That's success, not silence.

The dry run logged `Would ensure Dependency Dashboard`, confirming it's enabled via `config:recommended` on your config. But it only *would* — dry runs don't write, and with `has_issues: false` a real run has nowhere to put it. So: enabled in config, impossible in practice, until you flip Issues on.

It works end to end. Run [30704660158](https://github.com/hasToggle/spinor/actions/runs/30704660158) — all steps green in 1m19s, including **Mint an App installation token**, so the App credentials are validated for real.

`gh repo set-default` is fixed too — it was ambiguous because spinor is a fork, so `gh` couldn't tell whether you meant the fork or `hasToggle.dev`. Now pinned to `hasToggle/spinor`.

## What the run proved

```
Repo is onboarded          forkProcessing: "enabled"
bun:            28 files, 379 deps
github-actions:  2 files,   7 deps
DRY-RUN: Would ensure Dependency Dashboard
Repository finished        result: done, enabled: true, onboarded: true
```

The dashboard will be created on the next **non**-dry run now that Issues are on — the dry run correctly suppressed it.

## One real problem: the leftover branch is stranded

```
branch.isModified() = true   (branch=renovate/minor-updates)
result: "pr-edited"
```

`renovate/minor-updates` survives from the Cloud Runner era — its last commit is authored by `renovate[bot] <29139614+renovate[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`, Mend's identity. Your new app commits as `spinor-renovate[bot]`, a different author, so Renovate reads the branch as **modified by someone else** and deliberately refuses to touch it — that's the safety rule that stops it clobbering human edits to its own branches.

Left alone, that branch will sit there forever: never updated, never merged, never cleaned up. Its PR is already gone (only your PR #1 is open), so it's an orphan branch holding a stale `react-hook-form` bump from this morning.

Fix is to delete it and let the new app recreate it fresh on the next real run:

```sh
gh api -X DELETE repos/hasToggle/spinor/git/refs/heads/renovate/minor-updates
```

I haven't run that — deleting a branch is yours to approve. This is worth knowing generally: **any** hosted-app branch that outlives the migration is stranded the same way.

## Three smaller findings

**The `app-id` input is deprecated** — `create-github-app-token@v3` wants `client-id` now. It still works (the run passed), it's just a warning. Switching means storing the App's Client ID (`Iv23li…`) instead of the numeric App ID, so it needs a new secret from you. Happy to do it whenever you want; no rush.

**Dependabot alerts are off** — `No vulnerability alerts enabled for repo`. So the `vulnerability_alerts: read` permission is currently inert and Renovate can't prioritise security updates. `gh api -X PUT repos/hasToggle/spinor/vulnerability-alerts` enables it.

**Four dependencies are deprecated upstream**, found during extraction — two with real migration paths:

| Package | Notice |
|---|---|
| `@clerk/types` | superseded; import from `@clerk/shared/types` (Clerk core-3 upgrade guide) |
| `@rescale/nemo` | moved to `@zanreal/nemo`; the alias will stop receiving updates |
| `@react-email/components` | no longer supported |
| `@react-email/preview-server` | no longer supported |

Renovate's `replacements:all` preset (via `config:recommended`) may open replacement PRs for some of these automatically.

## Remaining

Everything is now live: app installed, secrets set, workflow on `main`, Issues on, schedule armed for every four hours. The only thing not yet exercised is a **real** (non-dry) run. Want me to fire one? It would create the Dependency Dashboard and — given `automerge: true`, no CI on PRs, and `allow_auto_merge: false` — potentially merge minor/patch updates straight to `main` without verification. That's the trade we discussed; I'd rather you say go than assume it.

name: Renovate

# Self-hosted replacement for the Mend Cloud Runner that drives hasToggle.dev.
# The bot identity is a GitHub App owned by the org (see docs/renovate.md);
# nothing here depends on a human's personal access token.

on:
  schedule:
    # Every four hours. This only controls how often Renovate wakes up and
    # looks — what it is allowed to open is decided by renovate.json.
    - cron: "0 */4 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      logLevel:
        description: Log level
        type: choice
        default: info
        options:
          - debug
          - info
          - warn
      dryRun:
        description: Dry run — resolve everything, write nothing
        type: boolean
        default: false

# Two overlapping runs duplicate branch work and can race each other's
# automerge step. Queue rather than cancel so a scheduled tick is never lost.
concurrency:
  group: renovate
  cancel-in-progress: false

# The job's own GITHUB_TOKEN does nothing here — every write goes through the
# App installation token minted below.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  renovate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Mint an App installation token
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v3
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RENOVATE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RENOVATE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          owner: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
          repositories: ${{ github.event.repository.name }}

      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # Renovate clones the repo itself with the App token; the checkout is
          # only here to give the action a workspace. Leaving the Actions
          # credentials behind in .git/config would serve no purpose.
          persist-credentials: false

      # Setting the env var only when the input is true keeps RENOVATE_DRY_RUN
      # absent on normal runs — an empty string is not a valid dryRun value.
      - name: Enable dry run
        if: ${{ inputs.dryRun }}
        run: echo "RENOVATE_DRY_RUN=full" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Renovate
        uses: renovatebot/github-action@v46.2.0
        with:
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          # Floats within the major so patches arrive without a config bump;
          # Renovate keeps the `uses:` pin above current by itself.
          renovate-version: 44
        env:
          # Global (self-hosted) config lives here rather than in a config file
          # so there is one place to read. The action forwards any RENOVATE_*
          # and LOG_LEVEL vars into the container.
          RENOVATE_PLATFORM: github
          RENOVATE_REPOSITORIES: ${{ github.repository }}
          # renovate.json is already committed, so the onboarding-PR flow is
          # dead weight — and requiring config means a run against a repo
          # without one fails loudly instead of silently doing nothing.
          RENOVATE_ONBOARDING: "false"
          RENOVATE_REQUIRE_CONFIG: required
          LOG_LEVEL: ${{ inputs.logLevel || 'info' }}

# Renovate (self-hosted)

`hasToggle.dev` is kept current by the Mend-hosted Renovate Cloud Runner. This
repo is not installed on that app, so it runs its own Renovate from
`.github/workflows/renovate.yml`, authenticated as an org-owned GitHub App.

Dependency policy itself lives in `renovate.json` at the repo root and is
unchanged from the upstream template. This document only covers the runner.

## Why a GitHub App rather than a PAT

- The token is a short-lived installation token (1 hour), minted per run, not a
  long-lived secret tied to a person's account.
- Pull requests are authored by the app, not by whoever's PAT it is, so
  `git log` and the PR list stay honest about what is automation.
- The app has its own API rate limit rather than sharing a human's.
- **Pull requests opened with an App token trigger other workflows.** Ones
  opened with the job's built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not — CI would never run on
  a Renovate PR, and with `automerge: true` that means merging unverified.

## One-time setup

### 1. Create the App

Requires org-owner rights on `hasToggle`. Create it at
<https://github.com/organizations/hasToggle/settings/apps/new> with the settings
below. Getting a permission wrong fails at run time rather than at setup, so it
is worth checking the read-back rather than trusting the clicks.

| Field                          | Value                                    |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| GitHub App name                | `spinor-renovate`                        |
| Homepage URL                   | `https://github.com/hasToggle/spinor`    |
| Webhook → Active               | **unchecked** (this runner polls)        |
| Where can this GitHub App be installed | Only on this account             |
| Subscribe to events            | none                                     |

Permissions ([source](https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/platform/github/)):

The form groups these under **Repository permissions** and **Organization
permissions**, and it labels several of them differently from the API keys used
in the manifest — which is worth knowing if you are cross-reading the two.

| Section      | Label on the form | API key               | Access       |
| ------------ | ----------------- | --------------------- | ------------ |
| Repository   | Administration    | `administration`      | Read         |
| Repository   | Checks            | `checks`              | Read & write |
| Repository   | Commit statuses   | `statuses`            | Read & write |
| Repository   | Contents          | `contents`            | Read & write |
| Repository   | Dependabot alerts | `vulnerability_alerts`| Read         |
| Repository   | Issues            | `issues`              | Read & write |
| Repository   | Metadata          | `metadata`            | Read         |
| Repository   | Pull requests     | `pull_requests`       | Read & write |
| Repository   | Workflows         | `workflows`           | Read & write |
| Organization | Members           | `members`             | Read         |

The two that are hardest to find are `statuses`, which the form calls **Commit
statuses**, and `vulnerability_alerts`, which it calls **Dependabot alerts**.
`members` is not in the Repository list at all — scroll down to the separate
Organization permissions section.

Two rows behave differently from the rest, which is expected rather than a
mis-click: **Metadata** offers no read-and-write option, and **Workflows**
offers no read-only one.

`Workflows: write` is what lets Renovate bump action versions inside
`.github/workflows/`; without it those updates fail while everything else
succeeds, which is a confusing way to find out.

Sanity check: `gh api /apps/renovate --jq .permissions` returns the permission
set of Mend's own hosted Renovate app. It matches the table above, plus
`emails: read` and `packages: read`, which the docs do not list as required.

After creating the app, verify what actually got saved rather than re-reading
the form:

```sh
gh api /apps/spinor-renovate --jq '{permissions, events}'
```

### 2. Generate a private key and note the App ID

On the app's settings page: **Generate a private key** (downloads a `.pem`) and
copy the numeric **App ID** from the top of the page.

### 3. Install the App on this repo

**Install App → hasToggle → Only select repositories → `spinor`**.

### 4. Add the secrets

```sh
gh secret set RENOVATE_APP_ID          --repo hasToggle/spinor --body '<app id>'
gh secret set RENOVATE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY --repo hasToggle/spinor < ~/Downloads/<app>.private-key.pem
```

Then delete the local `.pem` — it can always be regenerated, and a key sitting
in `~/Downloads` is a standing liability.

### 5. Verify

```sh
gh workflow run renovate.yml --repo hasToggle/spinor -f dryRun=true -f logLevel=debug
gh run watch --repo hasToggle/spinor
```

A dry run resolves every update and writes nothing. Look for
`Repository started` and a `DRY-RUN` line per branch it would have created. Then
run it again without `dryRun` to let it open real PRs.

## Repo settings this depends on

Two settings are off on this repo and both change how `automerge: true` behaves:

# Renovate (self-hosted)

`hasToggle.dev` is kept current by the Mend-hosted Renovate Cloud Runner. This
repo is not installed on that app, so it runs its own Renovate from
`.github/workflows/renovate.yml`, authenticated as an org-owned GitHub App.

Dependency policy itself lives in `renovate.json` at the repo root and is
unchanged from the upstream template. This document only covers the runner.

## Why a GitHub App rather than a PAT

- The token is a short-lived installation token (1 hour), minted per run, not a
  long-lived secret tied to a person's account.
- Pull requests are authored by the app, not by whoever's PAT it is, so
  `git log` and the PR list stay honest about what is automation.
- The app has its own API rate limit rather than sharing a human's.
- **Pull requests opened with an App token trigger other workflows.** Ones
  opened with the job's built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not — CI would never run on
  a Renovate PR, and with `automerge: true` that means merging unverified.

## One-time setup

### 1. Create the App

Requires org-owner rights on `hasToggle`. Create it at
<https://github.com/organizations/hasToggle/settings/apps/new> with the settings
below. Getting a permission wrong fails at run time rather than at setup, so it
is worth checking the read-back rather than trusting the clicks.

| Field                          | Value                                    |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| GitHub App name                | `spinor-renovate`                        |
| Homepage URL                   | `https://github.com/hasToggle/spinor`    |
| Webhook → Active               | **unchecked** (this runner polls)        |
| Where can this GitHub App be installed | Only on this account             |
| Subscribe to events            | none                                     |

Permissions ([source](https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/platform/github/)):

The form groups these under **Repository permissions** and **Organization
permissions**, and it labels several of them differently from the API keys used
in the manifest — which is worth knowing if you are cross-reading the two.

| Section      | Label on the form | API key               | Access       |
| ------------ | ----------------- | --------------------- | ------------ |
| Repository   | Administration    | `administration`      | Read         |
| Repository   | Checks            | `checks`              | Read & write |
| Repository   | Commit statuses   | `statuses`            | Read & write |
| Repository   | Contents          | `contents`            | Read & write |
| Repository   | Dependabot alerts | `vulnerability_alerts`| Read         |
| Repository   | Issues            | `issues`              | Read & write |
| Repository   | Metadata          | `metadata`            | Read         |
| Repository   | Pull requests     | `pull_requests`       | Read & write |
| Repository   | Workflows         | `workflows`           | Read & write |
| Organization | Members           | `members`             | Read         |

The two that are hardest to find are `statuses`, which the form calls **Commit
statuses**, and `vulnerability_alerts`, which it calls **Dependabot alerts**.
`members` is not in the Repository list at all — scroll down to the separate
Organization permissions section.

Two rows behave differently from the rest, which is expected rather than a
mis-click: **Metadata** offers no read-and-write option, and **Workflows**
offers no read-only one.

`Workflows: write` is what lets Renovate bump action versions inside
`.github/workflows/`; without it those updates fail while everything else
succeeds, which is a confusing way to find out.

Sanity check: `gh api /apps/renovate --jq .permissions` returns the permission
set of Mend's own hosted Renovate app. It matches the table above, plus
`emails: read` and `packages: read`, which the docs do not list as required.

After creating the app, verify what actually got saved rather than re-reading
the form:

```sh
gh api /apps/spinor-renovate --jq '{permissions, events}'
```

### 2. Generate a private key and note the Client ID

On the app's settings page: **Generate a private key** (downloads a `.pem`) and
copy the **Client ID** (`Iv23li…`) — not the numeric App ID, which
`actions/create-github-app-token` deprecated in v3.

### 3. Install the App on this repo

**Install App → hasToggle → Only select repositories → `spinor`**.

### 4. Add the secrets

```sh
gh secret set RENOVATE_APP_ID          --repo hasToggle/spinor --body '<app id>'
gh secret set RENOVATE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY --repo hasToggle/spinor < ~/Downloads/<app>.private-key.pem
```

Then delete the local `.pem` — it can always be regenerated, and a key sitting
in `~/Downloads` is a standing liability.

### 5. Verify

```sh
gh workflow run renovate.yml --repo hasToggle/spinor -f dryRun=true -f logLevel=debug
gh run watch --repo hasToggle/spinor
```

A dry run resolves every update and writes nothing. Look for
`Repository started` and a `DRY-RUN` line per branch it would have created. Then
run it again without `dryRun` to let it open real PRs.

## Repo settings this depends on

Two settings are off on this repo and both change how `automerge: true` behaves:

- **Issues are disabled.** `config:recommended` turns on the Dependency

  with `gh api -X PATCH repos/hasToggle/spinor -f has_issues=true`, or set
  `"dependencyDashboard": false` in `renovate.json` to opt out deliberately.
- **Auto-merge is disabled, `main` is unprotected, and no workflow runs on
  pull requests.** Renovate prefers GitHub's native auto-merge, which needs the
  repo setting on *and* something blocking the merge (a required check) for it
  to mean anything. With none of the three, `automerge: true` in
  `renovate.json` means patch and minor dependency updates land on `main` with
  no automated verification whatsoever — Renovate merges them itself on its
  next run. That may well be the intended trade for a repo reviewed locally,
  but it should be a decision rather than a discovery. To close it, add a CI
  workflow on `pull_request`, require it on `main`, and:

  ```sh
  gh api -X PATCH repos/hasToggle/spinor -f allow_auto_merge=true
  ```

- `forkProcessing: "enabled"` in `renovate.json` is load-bearing: this repo is a

- Cost is not a concern — the repo is public, so Actions minutes are free.
- To pause the bot without deleting anything, disable the workflow:
  `gh workflow disable renovate.yml --repo hasToggle/spinor`.

name: Renovate

# Self-hosted replacement for the Mend Cloud Runner that drives hasToggle.dev.
# The bot identity is a GitHub App owned by the org (see docs/renovate.md);
# nothing here depends on a human's personal access token.

on:
  schedule:
    # Every four hours. This only controls how often Renovate wakes up and
    # looks — what it is allowed to open is decided by renovate.json.
    - cron: "0 */4 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      logLevel:
        description: Log level
        type: choice
        default: info
        options:
          - debug
          - info
          - warn
      dryRun:
        description: Dry run — resolve everything, write nothing
        type: boolean
        default: false

# Two overlapping runs duplicate branch work and can race each other's
# automerge step. Queue rather than cancel so a scheduled tick is never lost.
concurrency:
  group: renovate
  cancel-in-progress: false

# The job's own GITHUB_TOKEN does nothing here — every write goes through the
# App installation token minted below.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  renovate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Mint an App installation token
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v3
        with:
          # client-id, not the numeric app-id: the latter is deprecated in v3.
          # Neither is actually secret — `gh api /apps/spinor-renovate` returns
          # the client id to anyone — but keeping it alongside the private key
          # keeps this step uniform.
          client-id: ${{ secrets.RENOVATE_APP_CLIENT_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RENOVATE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          owner: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
          repositories: ${{ github.event.repository.name }}

      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # Renovate clones the repo itself with the App token; the checkout is
          # only here to give the action a workspace. Leaving the Actions
          # credentials behind in .git/config would serve no purpose.
          persist-credentials: false

      # Setting the env var only when the input is true keeps RENOVATE_DRY_RUN
      # absent on normal runs — an empty string is not a valid dryRun value.
      - name: Enable dry run
        if: ${{ inputs.dryRun }}
        run: echo "RENOVATE_DRY_RUN=full" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Renovate
        uses: renovatebot/github-action@v46.2.0
        with:
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          # Floats within the major so patches arrive without a config bump;
          # Renovate keeps the `uses:` pin above current by itself.
          renovate-version: 44
        env:
          # Global (self-hosted) config lives here rather than in a config file
          # so there is one place to read. The action forwards any RENOVATE_*
          # and LOG_LEVEL vars into the container.
          RENOVATE_PLATFORM: github
          RENOVATE_REPOSITORIES: ${{ github.repository }}
          # renovate.json is already committed, so the onboarding-PR flow is
          # dead weight — and requiring config means a run against a repo
          # without one fails loudly instead of silently doing nothing.
          RENOVATE_ONBOARDING: "false"
          RENOVATE_REQUIRE_CONFIG: required
          LOG_LEVEL: ${{ inputs.logLevel || 'info' }}

However, `biome check --write` actually processes and modifies SVGs along with TypeScript and TSX files, so the `--write` flag is what enables the SVG handling.
